sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: Presents the front matter of the WHO interim guidance Digital Documentation of COVID-19 Certificates: Vaccination Status (DDCC:VS) — Technical Specifications and Implementation Guidance (27 August 2021, WHO/2019-nCoV/Digital_certificates/vaccination/2021.1), including copyright and licensing notices, the table of contents, acknowledgements, abbreviations, a glossary of technical and data-protection terms, and the Executive Summary. The Executive Summary defines the DDCC:VS as a digitally signed HL7 FHIR representation of COVID-19 vaccination events supporting two primary scenarios (Continuity of Care and Proof of Vaccination) across paper and digital formats without requiring a smartphone, and outlines the minimum policy, data, and service requirements (including Health Certificate Identifiers, a Generation Service, and a Registry Service).

sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces Section 1 by framing the global COVID-19 pandemic context and the need for countries to provide verifiable records of COVID-19 vaccination status that augment fraud- and loss-prone paper cards while respecting human rights, equity, ethical considerations, and data protection principles.

sections.title: Purpose of this document

summary.text: States the purpose of the document in Section 1.1: to provide a software-agnostic baseline set of requirements, a core data set, and a digital-signature approach based on free and open standards so Member States can design, adapt, and deploy interoperable DDCC:VS solutions in paper-plus-barcode or digital formats.

sections.extract: This document lays out an approach for creating a signed digital version of a vaccination record for COVID-19 based on a core data set of key information to be recorded, and an approach for the digital signature. The document leverages existing free and open standards, and is driven by the ethics, use cases and requirements for Digital Documentation of COVID-19 Certificates: Vaccination Status (DDCC:VS). sections.title: Trusting a DDCC:VS signature

summary.text: Explains the mathematical and operational basis for trusting a DDCC:VS signature in Section 6.3, noting how asymmetric cryptography guarantees authenticity and non-repudiation while PKI provides trusted public-key distribution and key revocation mechanisms.

sections.extract: The cryptographic strength of private–public key pairs is based on the mathematics of asymmetric cryptography, a process involving “one-way” mathematical functions, which are operations that are easy to compute in one direction but extremely hard to reverse. They provide a high level of security provided the private key is not compromised and remains available only to the entity performing the signing.

narratives.en: Figure 2, 'Different illustrative formats of DDCC:VS'. Two existing paper formats: 1, the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (the yellow card); 2, a national immunization home-based record, pictured as a COVID-19 vaccination record card. Then, grouped under Digital Documentation of COVID-19 Certificates: Vaccination Status: 3, a handwritten paper certificate with only an HCID that links to a DDCC:VS, or with a 2D barcode containing the full DDCC:VS core data set; 4, a PDF print-out certificate with only an HCID linking to a DDCC:VS, or with a 2D barcode containing the full core data set; 5, a DDCC:VS held on a smartphone. Formats 3-5 are pictured as a 'National COVID-19 Certificate' with a QR code.

Figure 3, 'Continuity of Care scenario': the vaccine is administered, the core data set is recorded on the DDCC paper certificate, and the record is then made available in digital form. Four lanes: subject of care, vaccinator, data entry personnel, DDCC holder. (1) The subject of care arrives at the care site; (2) the vaccinator vaccinates and (3) records core data set elements on a paper certificate, which the holder receives as Point A, a paper record of DDCC:VS. Is there a digital health solution at the care site? If no, (5) data entry personnel record the elements in a digital health solution. If yes, (4) the vaccinator records them in one; then, does the care site have Internet connectivity? Yes leads directly, and no via step 5, to Point B: the record of vaccination status is available in a digital form. End.

Figure 4, 'Continuity of Care scenario: Paper First use case (UC001)'. The Figure 3 workflow with one path highlighted: arrival (1), vaccination (2), recording on the paper certificate (3) which gives Point A, then no digital health solution at the care site, so data entry personnel record the data in a digital health solution (5), reaching Point B, the record available in digital form. Step 4 and the connectivity decision are greyed out.

Figure 5, 'Continuity of Care scenario: Offline Digital use case (UC002)'. The Figure 3 workflow with one path highlighted: arrival (1), vaccination (2), paper recording (3) giving Point A; a digital health solution is at the care site, so the vaccinator records the data in it (4); the site has no Internet connectivity, so data entry personnel record the data (5), reaching Point B. The direct 'no digital solution' and 'connected' branches are greyed out.

Figure 6, 'Continuity of Care scenario: Online Digital use case (UC003)'. The Figure 3 workflow with one path highlighted: arrival (1), vaccination (2), paper recording (3) giving Point A; a digital health solution is at the care site and the vaccinator records the data in it (4); the site has Internet connectivity, so the record goes directly to Point B, available in digital form. Step 5 by data entry personnel is greyed out.

Figure 7, 'The relationships between digital services for Proof of Vaccination'. A digital health solution submits a vaccination event to the DDCC:VS generation service, which returns a DDCC:VS. The HCID is provided by an existing national system or issued by the generation service. The generation service registers the DDCC:VS with the DDCC:VS registry service and may optionally store it in a DDCC:VS repository. Optional dashed links: an online status check between the registry service and the repository, and online verification of a DDCC:VS between an optional status checking application and the registry service. A note explains that the HCID, the unique identifier in a DDCC:VS, is used throughout these services and lets verifiers search for and retrieve a DDCC:VS.

Figure 8, 'Proof of Vaccination scenario': verification of a claim of vaccination. Four lanes: DDCC holder, verifier, national PHA, international PHA. (1) The holder presents the DDCC:VS; (2) the verifier receives the claim. Is cryptographic verification required? No leads straight to Point C, the decision on the verification. Yes: (3) the verifier uses a status checking application; perform check online? No leads to Point C. Yes: (4) the national PHA performs an online check with its DDCC registry service; check with international PHA? If yes, (5) the international PHA performs an online check with its registry service; either way (6) results are communicated back to the verifier, then Point C and End.

Figure 9, 'Proof of Vaccination scenario: Manual Verification use case (UC004)'. The Figure 8 workflow with one path highlighted: the holder presents the DDCC:VS (1), the verifier receives the claim (2), no cryptographic verification is required, and the verifier goes directly to Point C, the decision on the claim. All the status-checking and PHA steps are greyed out.

Figure 10, 'Proof of Vaccination scenario: Offline Cryptographic Verification use case (UC005)'. The Figure 8 workflow with one path highlighted: presentation (1), receipt of the claim (2), cryptographic verification required, the verifier uses a status checking application (3) and does not check online, going to Point C. The online PHA checks are greyed out.

Figure 11, 'Proof of Vaccination scenario: Online Status Check (National DDCC:VS) use case (UC006)'. The Figure 8 workflow with one path highlighted: presentation (1), receipt (2), cryptographic verification required, status checking application (3), online check performed by the national PHA against its DDCC registry service (4), no international check, results communicated back to the verifier (6), Point C. The international PHA step is greyed out.

Figure 12, 'Proof of Vaccination scenario: Online Status Check (International DDCC:VS) use case (UC007)'. The Figure 8 workflow with one path highlighted: presentation (1), receipt (2), cryptographic verification required, status checking application (3), national PHA online check (4), check with the international PHA, which performs an online check with its DDCC registry service (5), results communicated back to the verifier (6), Point C. The manual and offline branches are greyed out.

Figure 13, 'The chain of trust'. Three linked boxes: CSCA (country signing certificate authority) and DSC (document signer certificate), each with a private and a public key, and DDCC (Digital Documentation of COVID-19 Certificate), marked with a QR code. Above, 'Signing and issuing a DDCC' runs in steps 1-3 from CSCA through DSC to DDCC. Below, a dotted 'Verifying a DDCC' arc runs in steps 1-3 the other way, from DDCC back to CSCA.

Figure 14, 'How digital signatures work', under the heading Document Signing. A signer starts from a document (vaccination data); a hash is calculated from the document, giving the document hash; the hash is digitally signed with a private key, giving the signed hash; the signed hash is added to the document, giving a document with a digitally signed hash (the DDCC:VS).

Figure 15, 'How digital signature verification works'. The upper panel, Document Signing, repeats Figure 14: document, document hash, signed with the private key, signed hash added to the document to make the DDCC:VS. The signer sends the digitally signed document and the public key to the verifier. The lower panel, Document Validation: the verifier calculates a hash from the document and, using the public key, obtains the hash from the signed hash; the two values are compared, and a matching hash indicates a valid document, one that contains the information that was signed with the private key.

narratives.en: A screenshot of the PuTTY Key Generator window, given as an example of a key generation tool (Figure A4.2). The Key panel shows a highlighted RSA public key for pasting into an OpenSSH authorized_keys file, a key fingerprint beginning 'ssh-rsa 2048', and the key comment 'rsa-key-20210701', with empty passphrase fields. Actions offer Generate, Load, Save public key and Save private key; the parameters select an RSA key of 2048 bits.
narratives.fr: Capture d'écran de la fenêtre PuTTY Key Generator, présentée comme exemple d'outil de génération de clés (figure A4.2). Le panneau Key affiche en surbrillance une clé publique RSA à coller dans un fichier authorized_keys d'OpenSSH, une empreinte de clé commençant par « ssh-rsa 2048 » et le commentaire de clé « rsa-key-20210701 », avec des champs de phrase secrète vides. La section Actions propose les boutons Generate, Load, Save public key et Save private key ; les paramètres sélectionnent une clé RSA de 2048 bits.
narratives.es: Captura de pantalla de la ventana de PuTTY Key Generator, presentada como ejemplo de herramienta de generación de claves (figura A4.2). El panel Key muestra resaltada una clave pública RSA para pegarla en un archivo authorized_keys de OpenSSH, una huella digital de clave que comienza por «ssh-rsa 2048» y el comentario de clave «rsa-key-20210701», con los campos de frase de contraseña vacíos. La sección Actions ofrece Generate, Load, Save public key y Save private key; los parámetros seleccionan una clave RSA de 2048 bits.
narratives.ar: لقطة شاشة لنافذة برنامج PuTTY Key Generator، تُقدَّم كمثال على أداة لتوليد المفاتيح (الشكل A4.2). تعرض لوحة المفتاح (Key) مفتاحاً عاماً من نوع RSA مظللاً للصقه في ملف authorized_keys الخاص بـ OpenSSH، وبصمة مفتاح تبدأ بـ «ssh-rsa 2048»، وتعليق المفتاح «rsa-key-20210701»، مع حقول فارغة لعبارة المرور. وتوفر قسم الإجراءات (Actions) خيارات التوليد (Generate) والتحميل (Load) وحفظ المفتاح العام (Save public key) وحفظ المفتاح الخاص (Save private key)؛ وتحدد المعلمات مفتاح RSA بطول 2048 بت.
narratives.ru: Снимок экрана окна программы PuTTY Key Generator, приведенный в качестве примера средства генерации ключей (рисунок A4.2). В панели Key показаны выделенный открытый ключ RSA для вставки в файл authorized_keys OpenSSH, отпечаток ключа, начинающийся с «ssh-rsa 2048», и комментарий к ключу «rsa-key-20210701» с пустыми полями парольной фразы. В разделе Actions доступны кнопки Generate, Load, Save public key и Save private key; в параметрах выбран ключ RSA длиной 2048 бит.
narratives.zh: 作为密钥生成工具示例给出的PuTTY Key Generator窗口截图（图A4.2）。Key（密钥）面板显示一段高亮的RSA公钥（用于粘贴到OpenSSH的authorized_keys文件中）、以“ssh-rsa 2048”开头的密钥指纹以及密钥注释“rsa-key-20210701”，通行短语字段为空。Actions（操作）区域提供Generate（生成）、Load（加载）、Save public key（保存公钥）和Save private key（保存私钥）按钮；参数选择2048位RSA密钥。

narratives.en: Figure A6.1, the OpenHIE architecture. The OpenHIE component layer holds business domain services (logistics management information service, shared health record, health management information service, finance and insurance service) and registry services (terminology services, client registry, facility registry, health worker registry, product catalogue). Below it the interoperability services layer is a green 'Interoperability Layer' band with authentication, interlinking service and entity mapping. Along the bottom, point-of-service systems: mobile system, electronic medical record, health management information system, lab system, pharmacy system, logistics management information system, and finance and insurance system. Credited 'OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0'. The page's footnote says orange boxes mark the registries and repositories relevant to DDCC:VS; no orange marking is visible in this extracted image.
narratives.fr: Figure A6.1, l'architecture OpenHIE. La couche des composants OpenHIE regroupe les services de domaine métier (service d'information de gestion logistique, dossier de santé partagé, service d'information de gestion sanitaire, service des finances et de l'assurance) et les services de registres (services terminologiques, registre des clients, registre des établissements, registre des agents de santé, catalogue de produits). En dessous, la couche des services d'interopérabilité est représentée par une bande verte « Interoperability Layer » comprenant l'authentification, le service d'interconnexion et la mise en correspondance des entités. Au bas du schéma figurent les systèmes de point de service : système mobile, dossier médical électronique, système d'information de gestion sanitaire, système de laboratoire, système de pharmacie, système d'information de gestion logistique et système des finances et de l'assurance. Crédit : « OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0 ». La note de bas de page indique que des encadrés orange signalent les registres et dépôts pertinents pour le DDCC:VS ; aucun marquage orange n'est visible dans cette image extraite.
narratives.es: Figura A6.1, la arquitectura OpenHIE. La capa de componentes de OpenHIE contiene servicios de dominio de negocio (servicio de información de gestión logística, historia clínica compartida, servicio de información de gestión sanitaria, servicio de finanzas y seguros) y servicios de registro (servicios terminológicos, registro de clientes, registro de establecimientos, registro de trabajadores sanitarios, catálogo de productos). Debajo de ella, la capa de servicios de interoperabilidad es una franja verde «Interoperability Layer» con autenticación, servicio de interconexión y mapeo de entidades. En la parte inferior aparecen los sistemas en el punto de atención: sistema móvil, historia clínica electrónica, sistema de información de gestión sanitaria, sistema de laboratorio, sistema de farmacia, sistema de información de gestión logística y sistema de finanzas y seguros. Crédito: «OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0». La nota al pie de la página indica que los recuadros naranjas marcan los registros y repositorios pertinentes para DDCC:VS; en esta imagen extraída no se observa ningún marcado naranja.
narratives.ar: الشكل A6.1، بنية OpenHIE المعمارية. تضم طبقة مكونات OpenHIE خدمات مجال الأعمال (خدمة معلومات إدارة اللوجستيات، والسجل الصحي المشترك، وخدمة معلومات الإدارة الصحية، وخدمة التمويل والتأمين) وخدمات السجلات (خدمات المصطلحات، وسجل المراجعين، وسجل المرافق، وسجل العاملين الصحيين، ودليل المنتجات). وتحتها تظهر طبقة خدمات التشغيل البيني على هيئة شريط أخضر بعنوان «Interoperability Layer» يشمل المصادقة وخدمة الربط البيني ومواءمة الكيانات. وعلى امتداد الجزء السفلي تصطف أنظمة نقاط الخدمة: النظام المحمول، والسجل الطبي الإلكتروني، ونظام معلومات الإدارة الصحية، ونظام المختبر، ونظام الصيدلية، ونظام معلومات إدارة اللوجستيات، ونظام التمويل والتأمين. المصدر: «OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0». وتشير حاشية الصفحة إلى أن المربعات البرتقالية تميّز السجلات والمستودعات ذات الصلة بشهادة التوثيق الرقمي لحالة التطعيم (DDCC:VS)؛ غير أنه لا يظهر أي تمييز برتقالي في هذه الصورة المستخرجة.
narratives.ru: Рисунок A6.1 — архитектура OpenHIE. Уровень компонентов OpenHIE включает сервисы предметной области (информационную службу управления логистикой, общую медицинскую карту, информационную службу управления здравоохранением, финансово-страховую службу) и реестровые сервисы (терминологические сервисы, реестр пациентов, реестр медицинских учреждений, реестр медицинских работников, каталог продукции). Под ним расположен уровень сервисов интероперабельности в виде зеленой полосы «Interoperability Layer» с функциями аутентификации, службы связывания и сопоставления сущностей. Вдоль нижнего края показаны системы в точках оказания услуг: мобильная система, электронная медицинская карта, информационная система управления здравоохранением, лабораторная система, аптечная система, информационная система управления логистикой и финансово-страховая система. Источник: «OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0». В сноске на странице указано, что оранжевыми рамками выделены реестры и репозитории, относящиеся к DDCC:VS; на данном извлеченном изображении оранжевое выделение отсутствует.
narratives.zh: 图A6.1，OpenHIE架构图。OpenHIE组件层包含业务领域服务（物流管理信息服务、共享健康档案、卫生管理信息服务、财务与保险服务）和注册库服务（术语服务、客户注册库、机构注册库、卫生工作者注册库、产品目录）。其下方的互操作性服务层为绿色“Interoperability Layer”（互操作性层）横带，内含身份认证、互联服务和实体映射。底部排列着服务点系统：移动系统、电子病历、卫生管理信息系统、实验室系统、药房系统、物流管理信息系统以及财务与保险系统。署名：“OpenHIE 2020-05-28; CC BY 4.0”。页面脚注说明橙色框标出了与DDCC:VS相关的注册库和存储库；但在该提取图像中未见橙色标记。
